newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN, WALDORF REPEAT AS DINERS CLUB CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN, WALDORF REPEAT AS DINERS CLUB CHAMPIONS.

text.p: Tom Lehman and Duffy Waldorf retained their PGA Diners Club Championship, defeating the top-seeded team of Scott Hoch and Kenny Perry on Sunday at the $890,000 PGA Diners Club at PGA West.

Lehman and Waldorf, who needed to win a playoff Saturday to advance out of their round-robin group, claimed a 2 and 1 victory. They took control of Sunday's final match with birdies on the 15th and 16th holes.
Lehman's birdie on the 15th hole gave the defending champions a 1-up lead. Waldorf then birdied the 16th hole to give the duo a two-hole lead with two holes to play.
Needing to win the remaining two holes to tie the match, Hoch birdied the 17th hole with a 10-foot putt. But Lehman made a seven-footer for birdie to halve the hole and give his team the 2 and 1 win.

Hoch and Perry had cruised undefeated into the finals with a 3-0 record in their group. Lehman and Waldorf, meanwhile, won their final two matches in the round-robin after dropping the opener to Steve Jones and Rick Fehr on Thursday.
Those two teams, along with Justin Leonard and Mike Hulbert, went 2-1 in round-robin play, forcing a three-team playoff Saturday.
Fifth seeds Dottie Pepper and Juli Inkster won the LPGA Diners Club title with a 1-up victory over defending champions Kelly Robbins and Tammie Green in Sunday's final.
Pepper and Inkster gained a measure of revenge for a loss to Robbins and Green in the 1994 finals. They took the lead for good with Inkster's birdie on the 16th hole.
Pepper and Inkster reached the finals by defeating top seeds Karrie Webb and Michelle McGann in a playoff Saturday when Inkster birdied the third playoff hole.
The loss was the first in this tournament for Robbins and Green. The two-time champions had gone undefeated in round-robin play to improve their record to 9-0 in the three-year history of the event.
In the Senior Tour's final, Jim Colbert and Bob Murphy defeated Jay Sigel and Vicente Fernandez 3 and 1.
